messages:
sarah: heads up — we're getting a spike of 503s + elevated tail latency on Dedicated in na-east starting ~09:12 UTC. Customer complaints inbound. stack shows placement failures and some 429s when we try to retry.
kevin: which pool/cluster? any obvious recent deploys?
sarah: affects dedicated-pool-na-east-2 and a couple of small reserve pools. no app deploys reported. s3 logs + edge show a cluster of failures with allocator: 'placement_failed' and allocator health reporting stale heartbeats.
alyssa: looked at allocator logs — seeing repeated AZ_HEARTBEAT_MISMATCH entries and topology version drift. snip:
```
ERROR allocator: placement failed: AZ_HEARTBEAT_MISMATCH last_seen=2024-11-02T09:11:48Z topology_v=153 expected_v=156
WARN allocator: refusing to assign backstop group until topology sync
```
devon: that suggests topology-watcher didn't sync after leader election. control-plane's topology map is out of date so the scheduler thinks there are no compatible nodes. likely race during db leader failover. repro quick-check: `curl -s http://controlplane.internal/topology | jq '.na-east.nodes | .[] | {id, heartbeat_age: .last_heartbeat | now - . }'` (watch for >10s)
alloc-bot: :rotating_light: alert: dedicated.alloc.placement.failures rate=48/min (na-east), evictions=120 in 10m, topology_lag > 12s.
kevin: autoscaler status? are we blocked from launching more capacity because allocator returns empty sets?
alyssa: autoscaler attempted scale, but scale-policy 'backstop' has an inhibition when allocator returns no candidates. observed: scale triggered -> controller asked allocator -> allocator returned empty -> controller marked as failed scale attempt. so no new nodes came up.
sarah: customers hit: two high-throughput tenants did big bursts ~09:10 which saturated small pools and then allocator topology lag made the controller give up — combination of noisy tenant + topology lag.
devon: mitigation options (short):
1) temporarily widen placement policy to accept cross-AZ nodes for backstop group (less strict affinity)
2) force reroute of new incoming Dedicated requests to na-west pools while we heal na-east
3) restart topology-watcher on the control-plane leader to force a resync (small risk).
alyssa: steps i ran and recommend now:
- `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/v1/pools/dedicated-pool-na-east-2/actions/increase-backstop -d '{"factor":2}'`
- `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/v1/routing/reroute -d '{"from":"na-east","to":"na-west","selector":"dedicated"}'`
- `kubectl -n controlplane rollout restart deploy/topology-watcher --context=controlplane-leader`
(sanity: check `kubectl logs -n controlplane deploy/topology-watcher | tail -n 200` for successful "topology sync complete")
support-jess: drafting customer note: "We're investigating a regional placement issue in NA East causing some Dedicated requests to fail or see higher latency. We're routing new traffic to alternate capacity and expanding backstop pools. Engineers are on it; ETA next update in 30m." want anything added? :+1:
kevin: good. i'll coordinate cross-region reroute now. devon/alyssa keep me posted on restart and allocator behaviour. we'll run smoke tests after reroute (small curl/compare latency).
sarah: done initial reroute and increased backstop. seeing success traces for new requests hitting na-west. still seeing some 503s for retries hitting na-east — working through draining.
devon: after topology-watcher restart we got a full sync and allocator returned candidates. scale controller retried and launched 4 nodes. watch `dedicated.alloc.placement_success` for recovery.
kevin: action items: 1) postmortem (owner: devon), 2) add metric alarm for topology_lag > 5s that triggers autoscale unblock (owner: alyssa), 3) throttle guard/rate limit tweak for single tenant bursts (owner: sarah). support-jess will send customer update.
support-jess: sending update now. closing loop in 45m for impact numbers.
sarah: thanks — monitoring for residual errors. :thumbsup:
